identity.title: ALMA-IMF: XXI. N<SUB>2</SUB>H<SUP>+</SUP> kinematics in the G012.80 protocluster: Evidence of filament rotation and evolution

paper_type_evidence.quote: To study these processes in a massive cluster-forming environment, we focus on the G012.80 protocluster (hereafter G012), one of the 15 nearby massive protoclusters observed by the ALMA-IMF Large Program[^2] (cite: motte).
We use observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) telescope provided by the ALMA-IMF LP.

evidence.quote: Specifically, G012 is an active and massive (cite: motte) star-forming region centered on the W33 main clump, with a trigonometric parallax distance of 2.4 kpc (cite: distance) and a local standard of rest velocity of $V_{\mathrm{LSR}}$ = 37 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$ estimated from maser velocities (cite: immer2014).

Specifically, G012 is an active and massive (cite: motte) star-forming region centered on the W33 main clump, with a trigonometric parallax distance of 2.4 kpc (cite: distance) and a local standard of rest velocity of $V_{\mathrm{LSR}}$ = 37 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$ estimated from maser velocities (cite: immer2014).

question.value: Characterize dense gas kinematic processes, line-mass profiles, and evolutionary stages of the two main filaments (R1 and R2) in the G012.80 massive protocluster using N2H+(1-0) and complementary lines.

evidence.quote: We aim to characterize kinematic processes in the G012.80 protocluster. We primarily focus on the N$_2$H$^+$(1$-$0) emission to trace the dense and cold gas.
We aim to characterize the dense gas kinematics and key physical parameters in the protocluster, with particular emphasis on these two main filaments.

analysis_steps.goal: Data preparation, continuum subtraction, feathering, and S/N masking

method.value: Clean N2H+(1-0) observations with the ALMA-IMF pipeline, subtract continuum using imcontsub in emission-free channels, combine 7m, 12m, and TP data using feather, and construct pixel-by-pixel S/N maps from emission-free RMS noise.

evidence.quote: We use the `imcontsub` task to subtract the continuum emission from the N$_2$H$^+$ line emission. To estimate the continuum emission we consider only emission-free channels, in the range of 12 to 20 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$, where we apply a linear fit using `fitorder` = 0.
To recover the cloud emission at all available scales, we combine observations of the 7m and 12m arrays with total power data (TP). For this, we use the `feather` task.

analysis_steps.goal: Spectral line fitting of N2H+(1-0) hyperfine structure and complementary lines, and velocity component separation

method.value: Fit N2H+(1-0) hyperfine structure with 1 and 2 velocity components using PySpecKit specfit (n2hp_vtau), clean bad fits based on uncertainty thresholds, merge 1- and 2-component models into First (FVC) and Second (SVC) Velocity Components separated at 35.6 km s^-1, and fit single-Gaussian models to DCN, H41alpha, and SiO.

evidence.loc: Analysis of the N2H+ data cube
evidence.quote: We use the hyperfine line structure model provided by version V.1.0.1 of `PySpecKit` spectroscopic analysis toolkit (cite: pyspec).

Components below 35.6 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$ ($\sim$3,535 pixels) are assigned to the first velocity component (FVC), while those above ($\sim$2,984 pixels) are assigned to the second velocity component (SVC).
For tracers not previously modeled (DCN, H41$\alpha$, and SiO), we apply a single-Gaussian fit using `PySpecKit`.

key_parameters.value: 1-component guesses: Tex=31.3 K, tau=3.8, Vc=37 km s^-1, sigma=0.78 km s^-1; 2-component guesses: Tex=(15, 20) K, tau=(1, 3), Vc=(33, 37) km s^-1, sigma=(1.4, 0.47) km s^-1; limits: Tex (2.8, 150) K, tau (0.001, 10), Vc (25, 45) km s^-1, sigma (0.23, 5) km s^-1
Cleaning cuts: Vc and sigma errors < 0.3 km s^-1, sigma error != 0, tau/e(tau) > 1, tau <= 100; FVC/SVC velocity boundary = 35.6 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Errors in centroid velocity and velocity dispersion are mostly below 0.3 km s$^{-1}$, with only 5 and 26 pixels exceeding this value, respectively. Since this threshold is conservative relative to the N$_2$H$^+$ velocity resolution, we adopt it as the maximum allowed uncertainty for $\mathrm{V_c}$ and $\sigma$.
We therefore apply a mask requiring $\tau/e(\tau) > 1$, where $e(\tau)$ is the uncertainty in $\tau$.
We additionally impose an upper limit of $\tau = 100$ for each velocity component, removing 52 pixels above this threshold.

analysis_steps.goal: Moment maps and position-velocity (PV) diagram construction

method.value: Construct moment 0, 1, and 2 maps for FVC and SVC, identify main filaments R1 and R2, rotate N2H+ data cubes by 45 deg with respect to the protocluster center to vertically align filaments, and generate intensity-weighted PV diagrams parallel and perpendicular to the region.

evidence.quote: In Fig. [2](#fig:structures), we display the N$_2$H$^+$ integrated intensity (moment zero map, upper panels), velocity center (moment one map, middle panels), and velocity dispersion (moment two map, bottom panels) maps of the FVC and SVC.

We use the technique developed in (cite: gonzalez2019) to construct the N$_2$H$^+$ intensity-weighted position velocity diagrams (cite: gutierrez2021; yiyo2024; nico2024). To obtain better defined structures in PV space, we spatially rotate the N$_2$H$^+$ data cubes (45$^{\circ}$ respect to the protocluster center) by vertically aligning the most predominant filaments.

analysis_steps.goal: N2H+ column density, relative abundance X(N2H+), and total H2 mass estimation

method.value: Calculate N(N2H+) from fitted Tex, tau, and sigma for FVC and SVC after removing biased pixels, reproject N(N2H+) to the 0.83'' pixel scale of the Dell'Ova et al. (2024) N(H2) map, compute pixel-to-pixel ratio X(N2H+) = N(N2H+)/N(H2), find the mode of X(N2H+) via Freedman-Diaconis histogram binning, and convert N(N2H+) to total H2 mass.

To estimate this ratio, we reproject the N$_2$H$^+$ image to match the pixel scale of the H$_2$ data, which is slightly larger (with a pixel scale of 0.83$^{\ensuremath{''}}$). Subsequently we calculate the relative abundance map by taking the pixel-to-pixel ratio of the two maps:

We obtain a relative abundance of X(N$_2$H$^+$) = (0.93 $\pm$ 0.10) $\times$ 10$^{-10}$ (see Figure [4](#fig:ap_xfactmap), right panel), consistent with previous determinations (cite: caselli2002c; nico2024). This representative value is then applied to derive total H$_2$ mass.

analysis_steps.goal: Star formation rate (SFR), star formation efficiency (SFE), and core velocity estimation

method.value: Calculate SFR = M_cores / t_cores and SFE for prestellar and protostellar cores in R1 and R2 using core masses and classifications from Armante et al. (2024) and Motte et al. (2025), and derive new core line-of-sight velocities by fitting single-Gaussian models to average DCN and N2H+ spectra extracted within core ellipses.

evidence.quote: For the SFR and SFE estimates, we use the formalism outlined in (cite: tom2022) and consider the G012 core masses provided in (cite: motte2024). In R1 and R2, (cite: armante2024) and (cite: motte2024) identified a total of 16 cores.

To derive velocities, we fit the DCN and N$_2$H$^+$ emission with a single-Gaussian model (see Appendix [8](#sec:ap_linefitting)). The major and minor axes of each core (Tables [\[tab:ap_ourcores\]](#tab:ap_ourcores) and [\[tab:ap_dcncores\]](#tab:ap_dcncores)) define the region used to extract average spectra and estimate velocity centroids and mean fitted parameters.

key_parameters.value: Prestellar core lifetime t_cores = 1.2 Myr; protostellar core lifetime t_cores = 0.5 Myr (also tested 0.3 Myr); cloud mass uncertainty = 11%

evidence.quote: For our analysis, we adopt a prestellar timescale of 1.2 Myr, the expected value for prestellar cores in the mass range of 0.003 - 10 M$_{\odot}$ (cite: konyves2015). We also used protostellar lifetime of 0.5 Myr, assuming a low-mass protostellar regime around 0.5 M$_{\odot}$ (cite: tom2022).

findings_qualitative.value: Around 55% of the N2H+ spectra in G012 are well fitted by two velocity components and ~45% by a single velocity component, defining two main velocity structures (FVC and SVC) separated by ~2.5 km s^-1 at 35.6 km s^-1.

evidence.loc: Analysis of the N2H+ data cube
evidence.quote: The model fitting results show that G012 is characterized by two main velocity structures separated by $\sim$2.5 $\rm km\,s^{-1}$, which we define as the first velocity component (FVC) and the second velocity component (SVC).
Around 55$\%$ of the N$_2$H$^+$ spectra are well fitted by two velocity components, while the remainder are well described by a single velocity component.

findings_qualitative.value: N2H+ emission and relative abundance decrease at the center of G012 where H41alpha bubbles and C18O emission peak, consistent with N2H+ destruction by heating, free electrons, and CO from the central OB star cluster and H II regions.

evidence.quote: Given the high concentrations of H41$\alpha$ and C$^{18}$O in the center of G012, it is likely that the central H ii regions are heating the gas in the protocluster and destroying the N$_2$H$^+$ molecule through interactions with free electrons (cite: vigren2012) and with the CO molecule (cite: bergin1997; caselli2002b; caselli2012).

findings_qualitative.value: DCN(3-2) emission reveals V-shaped velocity structures at the top of R2 (coincident with a hot core and perpendicular SiO outflow) and toward the southern extended part of R1 and the central OB cluster, tracing potential localized gas inflows/accretion.

evidence.loc: DCN accretion evidence in the R2 filament and towards the central OB star cluster
evidence.quote: DCN emission in this region reveals a clear “V-shape” structure, features seen in other filaments undergoing accretion (cite: liu2019; bonne2020; bonne2023; yiyo2024; nico2024), coincident with the hot core location (see Fig. [8](#fig:dcn_pv), right panel), along with an SiO elongated feature perpendicular to the filament related with an outflow component (cite: armante2024).

We identify filamentary structures traced by DCN exhibiting signatures of potential accretion toward the center of the protocluster, where the OB stellar cluster is located and N$_2$H$^+$ is largely destroyed, suggesting that these structures may represent the remnants of a former hub-filament system.

findings_qualitative.value: Cores in G012 are kinematically coupled to the dense gas traced by N2H+ and DCN from which they are forming.

evidence.quote: Using N$_2$H$^+$ (1-0) and DCN (3-2) spectral lines, we estimate updated velocities for 48 previously identified cores. In general, the cores appear kinematically coupled to the dense gas traced by N$_2$H$^+$ and DCN from which they are forming.

claims.hypothesis: The R1 filament in the G012.80 protocluster is undergoing coherent rotation around its spine while gravity dominates over centrifugal forces.
claims.experiment: Constructed N2H+(1-0) PV diagrams, aligned the R1 filament along its ridgeline to measure the ridgeline-averaged transverse velocity gradient, derived the 3D gravitational acceleration from the line-mass profile, and applied a cylindrical rotation toy model to compute the centrifugal-to-gravitational force ratio Fc/Fg.
claims.result: R1 exhibits a helical PV pattern and a smooth transverse velocity gradient of 10.4 +/- 0.29 km s^-1 pc^-1 (rotational timescale ~0.1 Myr), with Fc/Fg < 1 across the filament radius (assuming cos(theta) = 1) but increasing with radius similarly to L1482-S.
claims.finding: R1 is undergoing coherent rotation that is subdominant compared to gravity, implying its most likely fate is to collapse into a state similar to R2.

evidence.quote: R1 exhibits a transverse velocity gradient of 10.4 km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{-1}$ and few dense cores. This velocity gradient is interpreted with a simple rotation toy model when combined with line-mass profile, and corresponds to a rotational timescale of $\sim\,0.1$ Myr.

evidence.loc: A filament rotation toy model applied to R1
evidence.quote: Assuming cos$(\theta)$ = 1, the R1 profile indicates that the filament is predominantly influenced by gravity rather than rotation, similar to the internal rotation pattern observed in the California L1482-S cloud.

We find that rotation in the R1 filament is subdominant compared to gravity, but as the radius increases the role of rotation increases, very similar to the behavior reported in the California L1482 filament (cite: gutierrez2021)

claims.hypothesis: The two main filaments in G012.80 (R1 and R2) represent different evolutionary stages of star formation within the same protocluster.
claims.experiment: Compared the N2H+ and DCN kinematics, PV diagrams, line-mass profiles, core populations (prestellar vs. protostellar), star formation rates (SFR), and star formation efficiencies (SFE) between R1 and R2 (both baseline boxes and FilFinder extended definitions).
claims.result: R1 has a transverse rotational velocity gradient, only 2 prestellar cores (0 protostellar), SFR = 4.24 +/- 0.29 M_sun Myr^-1, and SFE = (1.6 +/- 0.1) x 10^-3, whereas R2 has compact velocity structures (Delta V < 2 km s^-1), 5 prestellar and 9 protostellar cores, an SiO outflow, SFR = 55.3 +/- 6.93 M_sun Myr^-1, and SFE = (8.1 +/- 0.5) x 10^-3.
claims.finding: R1 is younger and still rotating with low star formation activity, while R2 has evolved to gravitational collapse with an order-of-magnitude higher SFR and SFE, showing that G012 hosts filaments at distinct evolutionary stages.

evidence.quote: Combining gas kinematics, core incidence, and the line-mass profiles, we suggest that R1 is younger and still rotating, while R2 has evolved to collapse with a higher SFR. G012 thus hosts filaments at different evolutionary stages.

Considering the R1 versus R2 differences in gas kinematics, core incidence, and estimated SFRs, we propose that R1 is still rotating and younger than the R2 filament, which has collapsed to a more efficient mode of star formation, likely by shedding its angular momentum.

claims.hypothesis: The filaments R1 and R2 in G012.80 have much higher line-mass profiles and densities than typical low-mass and intermediate-mass star-forming filaments, yet share universal rotational kinematic signatures across mass scales.
claims.experiment: Derived cumulative mass and power-law line-mass profiles lambda(omega) for R1 and R2 using N2H+ column density and relative abundance X(N2H+) = (0.93 +/- 0.10) x 10^-10, and compared them to L1482-S, ONC, Orion ISF, and G351.77.
claims.result: Line-mass profiles follow lambda(omega) = 5660 M_sun pc^-1 (omega/pc)^0.30 for R1 and lambda(omega) = 6943 M_sun pc^-1 (omega/pc)^0.20 for R2, up to 3 times denser than G351.77 and almost 30 times higher normalization at 1 pc than L1482-S.
claims.finding: R1 and R2 are highly dense dominant mass reservoirs (~60% of the protocluster mass in their extended structures), and the similarity in force-ratio profiles between R1 and L1482-S indicates common angular momentum evolution across almost 30x in line-mass scale.

evidence.quote: Line-mass profiles follow $\lambda$($\omega$) = 5660 M$_{\odot}$ pc$^{-1}$($\omega$/pc)$^{0.30}$ for R1 and $\lambda$($\omega$) = 6943 M$_{\odot}$ pc$^{-1}$($\omega$/pc)$^{0.20}$ for R2, which are much larger than those of typical low-mass filaments.

While the kinematic features appear similar between L1482 and R1, the line-mass profile normalization at 1 pc of R1 is almost 30 times higher than that of L1482. Hence, the similarities in the kinematics and the force-ratio profiles may indicate common angular momentum evolution of filaments across large ranges in mass and line-mass scales.

claims.hypothesis: Feedback from the central OB star cluster and H II regions destroys N2H+ in the center of G012.80, while DCN traces warmer gas inflows toward the cores and central cluster.
claims.experiment: Compared spatial distributions of N2H+(1-0), X(N2H+), C18O(2-1), DCN(3-2), H41alpha, and 1.3 mm/3 mm continuum, and constructed parallel DCN PV diagrams in the southern extension of R1 and central OB cluster region.
claims.result: N2H+ emission is absent and X(N2H+) drops near the central H41alpha bubbles and C18O peaks, while DCN shows coherent elongated structures with V-shaped PV patterns (velocity variations ~4 km s^-1) converging toward a massive core and the central H II bubble.
claims.finding: Central H II regions heat the gas and destroy N2H+ via free electrons and CO, whereas DCN survives and traces gas inflows feeding massive cores and the central cluster, possibly remnants of a former hub-filament system.

evidence.quote: Given the high concentrations of H41$\alpha$ and C$^{18}$O in the center of G012, it is likely that the central H ii regions are heating the gas in the protocluster and destroying the N$_2$H$^+$ molecule through interactions with free electrons (cite: vigren2012) and with the CO molecule (cite: bergin1997; caselli2002b; caselli2012).

We identify filamentary structures traced by DCN exhibiting signatures of potential accretion toward the center of the protocluster, where the OB stellar cluster is located and N$_2$H$^+$ is largely destroyed, suggesting that these structures may represent the remnants of a former hub-filament system.

why_this_data.value: G012 is an active, massive, evolved protocluster with H II regions, OB star clusters, and a high abundance of cores, making it an optimal testbed for studying high-mass star formation in a feedback-rich environment; N2H+(1-0) has lower depletion onto dust grains and a critical density (2.0-6.1 x 10^4 cm^-3) suited to probe cold dense gas.

evidence.quote: Detections of HC$_3$N, CO outflows, class I methanol masers, H ii regions, OB star clusters, and a high abundance of cores indicate that G012 is an optimal testbed for studying HMSF in an evolved protocluster, particularly the mechanisms regulating the distribution and kinematics of dense gas in a feedback-rich environment (cite: haschick1983; yu2019; xie2023; armante2024).

This nitrogen-bearing molecule is characterized by lower depletion levels onto dust grains and was first detected in the interstellar medium by (cite: thaddeus1975). For the N$_2$H$^+$(1-0) transition, the critical density ranges from 2.0 $\times$ 10$^4$ cm$^{-3}$ at 100 K to 6.1 $\times$ 10$^4$ cm$^{-3}$ at 10 K (cite: shirley2015), indicating the conditions under which this line becomes an effective tracer.

why_this_method.value: Combining 7m, 12m, and TP data via feather recovers missing large-scale flux and negative bowls; N2H+ column density is used to derive total H2 mass because the previous H2 dust column density map (Dell'Ova et al. 2024) lacks full spatial coverage over the main filaments; mode of X(N2H+) is used because it is stable under different binning and masking conditions.

evidence.quote: To recover the cloud emission at all available scales, we combine observations of the 7m and 12m arrays with total power data (TP). For this, we use the `feather` task. This combination also allows us to recover the missing flux, visible as negative bowls in the interferometric spectral data produced by the lack of zero-spacing.
In G012, previous estimates of the H$_2$ column density map (cite: pierre2024) do not provide the full spatial coverage achieved by the N$_2$H$^+$ map.

We determine representative N$_2$H$^+$ relative abundance values using the mode of its distribution, a choice motivated by its stability under different binning and masking conditions (see Appendix [11](#sec:ap_relative)).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single-component vs. two-component hyperfine N2H+ spectral fits: tested both across the cube and retained single-component fits where two-component fits produced poor fits for one component and single-component uncertainties were low.

evidence.quote: To address this, we refit the entire cube using two velocity components and evaluate whether the fits improve both inside and outside the previous selection criteria. For spectra containing a single velocity component, the two-component model often produces poor fits for either the bluest or reddest component. In these cases, we retain the single-component fit when its uncertainties are low and the fit quality is satisfactory.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using FilFinder automated skeletons vs. baseline visual box selections for the main kinematic analysis: rejected using full FilFinder skeletons for the baseline analysis because R2 splits into four branches at its lower end that cannot be reliably distinguished at current resolution.

evidence.quote: In some cases, FilFinder identifies more complex morphologies, particularly in the R2 filament, where most of the elongated structure follows a single main skeleton, but the lower part splits into approximately four possible branches (see right panel in Fig. [13](#fig:filfinder_detection)). Although one could select only the longest path as the main spine of the filament, we consider that it would not be fully reliable to claim that this represents the principal structure.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternative explanations for the R1 transverse velocity gradient (unresolved fibers/streamers, organized inflows along sub-filaments, or external H II region feedback): evaluated and rejected as primary explanations in favor of coherent large-scale filament rotation due to the smoothness and continuity of the transverse gradient and lack of V-shaped parallel PV structures in the upper R1 region.

evidence.quote: Among the possible explanations, a coherent rotation of the filament provides the most straightforward interpretation of the observed transverse velocity gradient. While localized inflows or feedback related perturbations may contribute to the kinematics in specific regions, particularly in the bottom and extended portion of R1 near to the H ii region, the overall smoothness and continuity of the transverse gradient along the filament are most consistent with a large scale rotational motion.

how_they_decided_enough.value: S/N threshold of 12 for N2H+ selected by testing various signal_cut values to exclude noisy/unresolved spectra; velocity uncertainty cut of 0.3 km s^-1 chosen because it is conservative relative to the 0.23 km s^-1 velocity resolution; tau/e(tau) > 2 mask chosen for relative abundance to balance uncertainty against pixel retention (removing ~7% of pixels).

evidence.quote: Testing various *signal_cut* values confirms that pixels below an $\mathrm{S/N}$ of 12 yield poor fits or large uncertainties in critical parameters like radial velocities errors.

Errors in centroid velocity and velocity dispersion are mostly below 0.3 km s$^{-1}$, with only 5 and 26 pixels exceeding this value, respectively. Since this threshold is conservative relative to the N$_2$H$^+$ velocity resolution, we adopt it as the maximum allowed uncertainty for $\mathrm{V_c}$ and $\sigma$.

evidence.loc: Technical considerations to estimate relative abundance
evidence.quote: To minimize the impact of large $\tau$ uncertainties while preserving most of the filamentary structure, we adopt the $\tau/e(\tau) > 2$ mask, which removes only $\sim$7$\%$ of the pixels.

limitations_admitted.value: Previous H2 column density map from Dell'Ova et al. (2024) has incomplete spatial coverage over the main filaments in G012.

evidence.quote: In G012, previous estimates of the H$_2$ column density map (cite: pierre2024) do not provide the full spatial coverage achieved by the N$_2$H$^+$ map.

limitations_admitted.value: Filament inclination angle relative to the plane of the sky is unknown, so 3D density, potential, acceleration, and rotational force ratios are 'apparent' POS quantities.

evidence.loc: Line-mass profiles and associated 3D model quantities
evidence.quote: All quantities are estimated in the POS since we do not have access to inclination information. We refer to these as “apparent” profiles following (cite: gutierrez2021).

limitations_admitted.value: SFR and SFE uncertainties only include core mass uncertainties from Motte et al. (2025) and do not include uncertainties in the adopted core lifetimes; furthermore, SFR and SFE estimates are lower limits due to core census incompleteness at the 2.4 kpc distance of G012.

evidence.quote: Errors were estimated solely from the mass uncertainties reported in the (cite: motte2024) catalog, without including possible uncertainties in the adopted timescales.

Our estimates of SFR and SFE should be regarded as lower limits, since they are based exclusively on the population of pre- and protostellar cores traced by some specific tracers. Unlike nearby star-forming regions, more distant regions such as G012 require more complete core censuses to provide accurate determinations.

limitations_admitted.value: V-shaped PV structures can arise from different kinematic configurations (e.g., rotation, outflows, or feedback perturbations) and do not uniquely trace accretion.

evidence.loc: DCN accretion evidence in the R2 filament and towards the central OB star cluster
evidence.quote: While such V-shaped structures are often interpreted as signatures of gas inflow, we note that similar PV morphologies can arise from different kinematic configurations (e.g., rotation or outflows), and therefore do not uniquely trace accretion.

limitations_admitted.value: Current angular resolution (~2.3'' / ~5.5-6 kau) cannot resolve sub-pc substructures such as fibers, forming cores, or accretion streamers, nor confirm whether the four branches at the bottom of R2 are independent substructures.

evidence.quote: Disentangling these other alternative scenarios will require higher resolution observations capable of resolving sub-pc structures such as fibers, forming cores, and accretion streamers, as well as detailed comparisons with simulations of feedback influenced filaments.
Higher-resolution data will be required to confirm whether these features correspond to dependent or independent substructures near the filament end.

referee_caveats_inferred: Applying a single constant N2H+ relative abundance X(N2H+) = 0.93 x 10^-10 across the entire protocluster to derive H2 filament masses may introduce systematic errors in line-mass profiles, since the paper itself shows X(N2H+) varies spatially due to feedback and heating near H II regions and hot cores.

Separating overlapping velocity components using a hard velocity boundary at 35.6 km s^-1 can artificially truncate wings or misassign components in regions with large velocity gradients or velocity dispersions.

The baseline R1 and R2 boxes (0.56 pc x 0.22 pc) isolate only sub-regions of the filaments; when extended FilFinder masks are used, R1 contains protostellar cores and the SFE ratio between R2 and R1 drops from ~5 to ~1.5.
